bib.title: Discovering Multiagent Learning Algorithms with Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Discovering Multiagent Learning Algorithms with Large Language Models", Zun Li, John Schultz, Daniel Hennes, Marc Lanctot (Google DeepMind), arXiv 2602.16928v3 (cs.GT), 7 May 2026. Preprint.

COVERAGE: Extracted text is 113,245 chars. I read the body in full (0-~50,000: abstract, method, experiments, related work, limitations, references). I read the appendix ablation specs, Tables 1-2, game-suite rationale, the 7.5 random-game evaluation, and the prompt/config listings (~77,000-108,000). I skimmed the code listings 3-6 (~50,000-77,000 and 84,900-86,500), which are long algorithm source, and the game descriptions 7.3.1-7.3.5. I did not read the figure text beyond the captions. Figures 3-6 are plots with no extractable numbers.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Claim: LLM-evolved algorithms overfit, and a train/test ablation audit separates the parts that generalize from the parts that only fit the training games. This is the source's main method.
   number: Test IQM change on removing the LLM's secondary features: no_volatility -0.029, no_boost -0.204. Train IQM change: -0.842 and -0.954.
   setup: VAD-CFR. Train = 4 games (3p Kuhn, 2p Leduc, 4-card Goofspiel, 5-sided Liar's Dice). Test = 14 larger or other games. Scores are IQM of log10 exploitability improvement versus the raw discovery. All runs are deterministic with exact exploitability.
   quote: "removing secondary features such as EWMA volatility tracking (no_volatility, s_train = −0.842, s_test = −0.029) or instantaneous regret boosting (no_boost, s_train = −0.954, s_test = −0.204) degrades training fit while having only marginal effects on held-out generalization (Table 1)."
   where: Section 4.3.1, p.7
2. Claim: Three structural pieces carry generalization in VAD-CFR. Removing any one causes a large collapse on the held-out games.
   number: Test IQM when removed: warm-start -2.003, asymmetric discount -1.065, optimistic prediction -0.905.
   setup: same as claim 1 (Table 1).
   quote: "Hard Warm-Start (s_train = −5.256, s_test = −2.003): The most critical feature discovered by the LLM is a strict 500-iteration suspension of all policy averaging."
   where: p.7. Table 1 is on p.6.
3. Claim: Distilling to the three core pieces (WOP-CFR) matches or beats the raw discovery on held-out games, with much less code and complexity. It does worse on the training games.
   number: Test IQM +0.119, Train IQM -0.802, Total -0.073. WOP-CFR ranks top-3 on all 18 games and lowest exploitability on 14. VAD-CFR is top-3 on all 18 and lowest on 15.
   setup: 18-game suite (Poker, Goofspiel, Liar's Dice, Blotto, Battleship variants). Baselines are CFR, CFR+, LCFR, DCFR, PCFR+, DPCFR+, HS-PCFR+(30). K=1000 iterations. Seed program is CFR+.
   quote: "this distilled variant achieves a +0.119 Test IQM improvement over the raw VAD-CFR discovery."
   where: Section 4.3.2, p.8
4. Claim: The same pattern holds for PSRO. The ORM+ loop is the engine. The hybrid blending and annealing are overfit artifacts, because removing them slightly improves test scores.
   number: no_blending_pure train -2.292, test -1.268. no_blending_orm test +0.020. no_annealing test +0.016. eval_as_train test -0.541. PM-PSRO test +0.059.
   setup: PSRO with an exact best-response oracle, exploitability at the 100th PSRO iteration. Baselines are Uniform, Nash (LP), AlphaRank, PRD, RM. Seed program is Uniform.
   quote: "removing the hybrid blending and dynamic scheduling each independently improves Test IQM (+0.020, +0.016), confirming they are overfitted artifacts rather than generalization drivers."
   where: Section 4.4.1, p.9. Table 2 is on p.28.
5. Claim: SHOR-PSRO and PM-PSRO both rank top-3 on every one of the 18 games and have the lowest exploitability on 12. They also beat all baselines on random constant-sum normal-form games.
   number: 1000 random games per (N,A) configuration. Six configurations: 3-5 players, 20-100 actions. 50,000 bootstrap resamples for 95% CIs.
   setup: Section 7.5. N>=3 only, because LP-Nash trivially wins at N=2. Gaussian and Uniform payoffs.
   quote: "SHOR-PSRO and PM-PSRO dominate all baselines across every (N,A) tested."
   where: p.10 and Section 7.5, p.32-33
6. Claim: The authors frame LLM evolutionary search as a proposal mechanism inside a human-in-the-loop pipeline: propose, audit with a train/test ablation, then a human distills.
   number: none
   quote: "LLM-driven evolutionary search is most useful as a proposal mechanism embedded in a human-in-the-loop pipeline: the LLM proposes candidate combinations of mechanisms, train-test ablation surfaces which generalize, and the researcher distills the survivors."
   where: Section 6, p.11
7. Claim: The search loop itself is simple. It samples a parent by fitness, an LLM mutates its code, the candidate is scored on proxy games, and valid candidates join the population.
   number: none
   setup: AlphaEvolve with Gemini 2.5 Pro. Multi-objective scoring: one objective is picked at random each round. Fitness is the negative final exploitability on 4 training games plus their average. The reported algorithm is chosen by average score. The prompt template randomly mixes task-instruction variants (e.g. combine strengths, unconventional change, new idea). It adds "Focus on simplifying the code" with probability 0.2, and a "lazy_prompt" nudge with probability 0.5 (Listing 10).
   quote: "The candidate is executed on a set of proxy games and scored by final negative exploitability; valid candidates are added to P and the loop repeats."
   where: Section 3.1, p.4. Section 3.4, p.5. Listing 10, p.36-37.
8. Claim: The search space is a fixed interface of evolvable classes with fixed signatures. This keeps mutations valid and comparable to known baselines, and standard CFR and the other baselines are special cases of it.
   quote: "This search space is expressive enough to encompass the entire family of known CFR variants as special cases"
   where: Section 3.2, p.4

LIMITS
- Authors' own list (p.11):
  - Single AlphaEvolve trajectory. No variance over independent runs. Stability of the distilled components across runs is unverified.
  - Headline IQM is mostly within-family generalization. The train and test sets share three game families. Blotto and Battleship are the out-of-family games.
  - Distillation needs human judgment, so it is not autonomous.
  - No convergence guarantees.
  - Only tabular baselines. No deep CFR or neural auto-curricula PSRO.
  - Exact exploitability limits games to under 350K information states.
  - Dependence on the LLM backbone and prompt is open.
- Deterministic algorithms with exact evaluation, so there are no seed or noise issues in the benchmark. The only random element is the one evolution run.
- The test games partly overlap the training games' families, and the train/test split was chosen manually.
- WOP-CFR is worse than VAD-CFR on train (-0.802), so "better" is on held-out games only.
- Small effect sizes: test +0.119 and +0.059 in log10 units, and several PSRO ablations are within ±0.02. No CIs on the main IQM tables. CIs appear only in 7.5.
- Compute and cost of the evolutionary run are not reported (not found in the text I read).
- The backbone, Gemini 2.5 Pro, has dated.

BUILDS ON: AlphaEvolve (Novikov et al., 2025); CFR (Zinkevich et al., 2007); CFR+ (Tammelin, 2014); DCFR (Brown and Sandholm, 2019b); PCFR+ (Farina et al., 2021); PSRO (Lanctot et al., 2017); IQM (Agarwal et al., 2021); OpenSpiel (Lanctot et al., 2019); AutoML-Zero (Real et al., 2020); Lu et al., 2024 (LLM-discovered preference-optimization losses); Chen et al., 2023 (Lion optimizer search); Oh et al., 2025 (discovering RL algorithms).

CODE
- Listing 1 (p.15) is the evolvable interface: three classes, each with one method (`update_accumulate_regret`, `get_updated_current_policy`, `update_accumulate_policy`), each taking `info_state_node, iteration_number, ...`. Only these are mutated. Listing 2 (p.15-16) has the two PSRO solver classes.
- The ablation score, as printed in Section 4.2: s_g = log10(Expl_raw) - log10(Expl_abl). A positive score means the simplified version beat the raw one. Aggregate with IQM over train, test and total.
- Prompt knob (Listing 10, p.37): `"Focus on simplifying the code, instead of adding new functionality."`, with weight 0.2.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.5): CFR variant exploitability curves on train and test games. This is the quickest check of the "competitive on held-out games" claim.
- Fig 2 (p.8): the same for PSRO.
- Fig 3-4 (p.38-39): all 18 games. Fig 5-6 (p.40): random normal-form games with bootstrap CIs.
- Table 1 (p.6) and Table 2 (p.28): train versus test ablation scores. Table 1 is the most useful for teaching, since the train/test gap shows overfit components directly.

PLACEMENT
Mostly peripheral to loop engineering. It is a research-domain evolutionary search loop, not an agent harness. Two pieces fit the course:
(a) The main fit is 03 scorekeeper, or 09 failure modes and guardrails, on the overfit-to-the-metric failure. A fitness score on the training set rewards complexity that does not transfer. The guardrail is a held-out split plus a component ablation audit. Claims 1 and 4 plus the Table 1 numbers support one added sentence or one references row.
(b) A secondary fit is 02 loop shapes or 08 self-improving loops, citing the propose / evaluate-on-proxy / select loop (claim 7) and the "human-in-the-loop distiller" conclusion (claim 6). 08 is over length, so use a citation and references row only, with no new prose.
Not relevant to 05 long-running loops or 07 autonomy ladder, apart from claim 6, where the limitation says distillation is "human-in-the-loop, not fully autonomous". Treat the source as "sharpens" for the existing overfitting or held-out-eval content.

PROBLEMS: Extraction is clean apart from PDF word-joining in the abstract and some math symbols. Figure axes are garbled, as expected. No embedded instructions found. The prompt listings contain imperative text that is part of the paper's LLM prompts, and I did not act on it. Files: I wrote the extracted text to /tmp/li.txt. No repo files were edited.
